mainEntity.name: What makes Simply Enak different from other food tours?

acceptedAnswer.text: We're locals who grew up eating at these places. You'll meet Aunty Lim, who's been making laksa since 1982. You'll visit stalls where we've eaten for years, and hear the stories behind every dish. We've been doing this since 2011 — the vendors know us, and you'll feel the difference.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

mainEntity.name: Can I join a tour alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Solo travellers are common on our join-in tours. You'll be with a small group of up to 9 people, which makes it easy to meet other guests. Most solo guests say it's one of the best things they did on the trip.

mainEntity.name: What areas of Malaysia do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: We run food tours in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. Each city has its own food identity: KL for urban hawker culture and multicultural street food, Penang for Peranakan heritage and char kway teow.

mainEntity.name: How do I book a tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The simplest way is to WhatsApp us on +60 17-287 8929. Tell us which tour you're interested in, your group size, and preferred dates. We'll confirm availability and send you all the details. You can also fill in the form on any tour page and we'll get back to you within 3 hours.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

Meeting point details are sent when you confirm your booking. In most cases it's a landmark near the first hawker area — easy to find by taxi or Grab. Look for the Simply Enak guide wearing a blue badge. If you're running late, WhatsApp us on +60 17-287 8929.

No formal dress code, but wear light, breathable clothing — Malaysia is 30°C+ year-round. Comfortable closed-toe shoes are better than sandals on market floors. If we walk past a mosque or temple, covered shoulders and knees show respect to the community.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

@graph.description: Explore Penang's UNESCO-listed food heritage with local guides. Discover hawker centers, heritage shophouses, and family recipes.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Penang for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Best: December-February (cooler). Food festivals: April (George Town Festival), August (Hungry Ghost Festival).

mainEntity.name: Are your Penang food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Penang food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

itemListElement.name: Market Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

mainEntity.name: What makes Simply Enak different from other food tours?

acceptedAnswer.text: We're locals who grew up eating at these places. You'll meet Aunty Lim, who's been making laksa since 1982. You'll visit stalls where we've eaten for years, and hear the stories behind every dish. We've been doing this since 2011 — the vendors know us, and you'll feel the difference.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

mainEntity.name: Can I join a tour alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Solo travellers are common on our join-in tours. You'll be with a small group of up to 9 people, which makes it easy to meet other guests. Most solo guests say it's one of the best things they did on the trip.

mainEntity.name: What areas of Malaysia do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: We run food tours in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. Each city has its own food identity: KL for urban hawker culture and multicultural street food, Penang for Peranakan heritage and char kway teow.

mainEntity.name: How do I book a tour?

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

@graph.description: Explore Penang's UNESCO-listed food heritage with local guides. Discover hawker centers, heritage shophouses, and family recipes.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Penang for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Best: December-February (cooler). Food festivals: April (George Town Festival), August (Hungry Ghost Festival).

mainEntity.name: Are your Penang food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Penang food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

itemListElement.name: Market Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

mainEntity.name: What makes Simply Enak different from other food tours?

mainEntity.name: How long are the food tours?

mainEntity.name: Are the tours suitable for children?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely! We love sharing Malaysian food heritage with families. We can adjust portions, spice levels, and pacing to make it enjoyable for children while teaching them about Malaysian culture.

mainEntity.name: What makes Simply Enak different from other food tours?

acceptedAnswer.text: We're locals who grew up eating at these places. You'll meet Aunty Lim, who's been making laksa since 1982. You'll visit stalls where we've eaten for years, and hear the stories behind every dish. We've been doing this since 2011 — the vendors know us, and you'll feel the difference.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

mainEntity.name: Can I join a tour alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Solo travellers are common on our join-in tours. You'll be with a small group of up to 9 people, which makes it easy to meet other guests. Most solo guests say it's one of the best things they did on the trip.

mainEntity.name: What areas of Malaysia do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: We run food tours in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. Each city has its own food identity: KL for urban hawker culture and multicultural street food, Penang for Peranakan heritage and char kway teow.

mainEntity.name: How do I book a tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The simplest way is to WhatsApp us on +60 17-287 8929. Tell us which tour you're interested in, your group size, and preferred dates. We'll confirm availability and send you all the details. You can also fill in the form on any tour page and we'll get back to you within 3 hours.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Penang for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Best: December-February (cooler). Food festivals: April (George Town Festival), August (Hungry Ghost Festival).

mainEntity.name: Are your Penang food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Penang food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

itemListElement.name: Market Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

itemListElement.name: Market Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

mainEntity.name: Can I join a tour alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Solo travellers are common on our join-in tours. You'll be with a small group of up to 9 people, which makes it easy to meet other guests. Most solo guests say it's one of the best things they did on the trip.

mainEntity.name: What areas of Malaysia do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: We run food tours in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. Each city has its own food identity: KL for urban hawker culture and multicultural street food, Penang for Peranakan heritage and char kway teow.

mainEntity.name: How do I book a tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The simplest way is to WhatsApp us on +60 17-287 8929. Tell us which tour you're interested in, your group size, and preferred dates. We'll confirm availability and send you all the details. You can also fill in the form on any tour page and we'll get back to you within 3 hours.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

itemListElement.name: Couples Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Penang food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What makes Simply Enak different from other food tours?

acceptedAnswer.text: We're locals who grew up eating at these places. You'll meet Aunty Lim, who's been making laksa since 1982. You'll visit stalls where we've eaten for years, and hear the stories behind every dish. We've been doing this since 2011 — the vendors know us, and you'll feel the difference.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

mainEntity.name: Can I join a tour alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Solo travellers are common on our join-in tours. You'll be with a small group of up to 9 people, which makes it easy to meet other guests. Most solo guests say it's one of the best things they did on the trip.

mainEntity.name: What areas of Malaysia do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: We run food tours in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. Each city has its own food identity: KL for urban hawker culture and multicultural street food, Penang for Peranakan heritage and char kway teow.

mainEntity.name: How do I book a tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The simplest way is to WhatsApp us on +60 17-287 8929. Tell us which tour you're interested in, your group size, and preferred dates. We'll confirm availability and send you all the details. You can also fill in the form on any tour page and we'll get back to you within 3 hours.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Penang for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Best: December-February (cooler). Food festivals: April (George Town Festival), August (Hungry Ghost Festival).

mainEntity.name: Are your Penang food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Penang food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

itemListElement.name: Market Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Kuala Lumpur for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Year-round destination. Best weather: March-April, August-September. Avoid: Monsoon season (November-January).

mainEntity.name: Are your Kuala Lumpur food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Kuala Lumpur food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

mainEntity.name: What's the best time to visit Penang for food?

acceptedAnswer.text: Best: December-February (cooler). Food festivals: April (George Town Festival), August (Hungry Ghost Festival).

mainEntity.name: Are your Penang food tours suitable for vegetarians?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We offer dedicated vegetarian food tours and can adapt most tours for dietary restrictions. Just let us know when booking and we'll ensure you have plenty of delicious options.

mainEntity.name: How much walking is involved in the Penang food tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tours cover about 2-3 kilometers over 4-5 hours, with plenty of stops to eat and rest. We walk at a leisurely pace and can accommodate most fitness levels.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to book in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we recommend booking at least 2-3 days in advance. Our tours are limited to 8 people to keep the experience intimate, and they often fill up 1-2 weeks ahead during peak season.
Tours run rain or shine! We have covered walkways and indoor stops along the route. In case of severe weather, we'll reschedule or provide a full refund.

itemListElement.name: Market Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

itemListElement.name: Market Food Tour around Kuala Lumpur

mainEntity.name: How many people join each tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: Maximum 9 guests per join-in tour. Small enough that you can actually talk with the vendors, ask questions, and eat without feeling rushed. Private tours go at your own pace with your own group.

We understand that plans change. Cancel up to 48 hours before your tour for a full refund. Cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable, but we're happy to reschedule to another date if we have availability. For private tours, please contact us directly.

mainEntity.name: I'm vegetarian — will there be enough to eat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Malaysia has deep Buddhist and Hindu vegetarian traditions, so yes. Every tour has strong plant-based options. Tell us when you book and your guide will call out vegetarian dishes at every stop. You won't go hungry.

Yes. All Simply Enak tours are fully halal-friendly. Malaysia's hawker culture is predominantly halal and we specifically choose stalls that meet this standard. If you have specific concerns, just ask when you book.

Around 2–3 km over 4–5 hours, with frequent stops to eat, listen, and ask questions. The pace is relaxed. Terrain is generally flat in both KL and Penang hawker areas. If anyone in your group has mobility concerns, let us know and we'll plan accordingly.

Comfortable shoes, light clothing, and an appetite. Cash in ringgit is useful (RM 50–100) as some stalls are cash-only. A small bag for your phone and camera. We provide drinks at each stop, but bringing a water bottle helps in the heat.

Most tours start in the morning — typically 9:00 or 10:00 am — when hawker centres are at their liveliest and the food is freshest. The KL nightlife tour starts in the evening. Exact times are confirmed when you book.

mainEntity.name: What makes Simply Enak different from other food tours?

acceptedAnswer.text: We're locals who grew up eating at these places. You'll meet Aunty Lim who's made laksa since 1982, visit family-run stalls where we've eaten for generations, and hear stories behind every dish. Come as a guest, leave as family.
Yes! We can accommodate vegetarian, halal, gluten-free, and other dietary needs. Just let us know when booking and we'll make sure your guide knows what to call out at each stop.

mainEntity.name: How long are the food tours?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our heritage food tours range from 4-5 hours, including walking through neighborhoods and meeting vendors. We pace ourselves based on your group's interests and energy.

mainEntity.name: Are the tours suitable for children?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely! We love sharing Malaysian food heritage with families. We can adjust portions, spice levels, and pacing to make it enjoyable for children while teaching them about Malaysian culture.
